🛑 **CORRECTION: ALEX'S TWO 2026-08-14 REPORTS CAME FROM TWO DIFFERENT MACHINES WITH TWO DIFFERENT AGENTS, AND THIS SESSION TREATED THEM AS ONE.** Anthony, relaying Alex's own question about which feedback was being discussed, then clarifying the setup:

```
              MACHINE            OS       AGENT    PROJECTS        REPORT
work          work laptop        macOS    Claude   real work       the 5 ideas
home          personal laptop    macOS    Grok     personal        the Grok feedback.md
```

⚠️ ON `basis`: the enum offers only `measured` or `forecast`. The machine/agent/OS attribution is REPORTED — Anthony relaying Alex — not observed by reflow2. The kit VERSIONS below are genuinely measured. Marked `measured` because most load-bearing content is, with the distinction stated here rather than lost to a missing enum value.

⚠️ WHAT THIS SESSION GOT WRONG. `fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14` describes the Grok file as *"a Grok 4.6 session on one of Alex's projects"*, which reads as the same context that produced the five ideas. It is not. Any inference treating the two as evidence about ONE install is unsound as stated.

═══ THE STALE-KIT CLAIM, RESTATED HONESTLY ═══

This session repeatedly said *"three independent signals that consumers run stale kits"*, implying mutual reinforcement about one user. **They are three SEPARATE installs, each stale:**
```
work / Claude / macOS ..... two of five notes describe behaviour fixed in
                            #172/#174 -> INFERRED stale, NEVER MEASURED
home / Grok / macOS ....... kit-version.json reads 0.11.0 / 0ec473e,
                            a 2026-07-25 tarball -> MEASURED
this dev machine / Linux .. kit stamp 0.28.0 / e2b05c7 -> MEASURED
```
⇒ WEAKER as evidence about Alex — only his HOME install was measured, and the five ideas came from WORK. STRONGER as evidence about the UPDATE PATH: three machines, at least two install routes, three versions, none current. **Systemic, not one person forgetting.**

🎯 THE VERSION QUESTION NEEDS A MACHINE. Anthony texted Alex asking what `reflow2 --version` says; **he has two installs and the answer differs.** The WORK one matters most — it produced the five ideas behind `epoch:a-project-is-set-up-right-on-the-first-run` and has never been measured.

═══ ⭐⭐ IT IMMEDIATELY FOUND A DEFECT IN WORK SHIPPED THE SAME HOUR ═══

`cap:init-asks-which-harness` had just been built with a deliberate decision: **`grok` is NOT a registry entry**, because Grok CLI reads `.mcp.json` and a second entry would write the same file twice under two names. A test asserted it. **The reasoning was right and the ergonomics were hostile: `--harness=grok` returned `error: unknown harness 'grok'` and exit 1** — the install REFUSING a correct answer from a user naming his own tool. Learning that Alex runs Grok at home is what surfaced it.

FIXED the same hour, keeping the reasoning and dropping the hostility: `HARNESS_ALIASES = {"grok": "claude"}` resolves the name without adding a config, the prompt line reads *"Claude Code (also read by Grok CLI — choose this for Grok)"*, and `grok,claude` collapses to one config rather than erroring. Four tests guard it, including that every alias points at a real harness and that no name is both an alias and an entry.

📌 **A GENERAL LESSON, since `rule:a-lesson-is-generalised-before-it-is-built` now exists:** a registry that is CORRECT about what to install can still be WRONG about what to accept. The two are different questions — what files does this harness need, and what might a user call it — and collapsing them refuses real answers.

═══ 📌 ENVIRONMENT FACTS NEW TO THE DESIGN ═══

  · **EVERY SECOND-USER REPORT REFLOW2 HAS EVER RECEIVED IS FROM macOS**, and **every measurement reflow2 has ever made is on Linux** — including all of 2026-08-14's installer runs and the harness wizard itself. Whether `tools/install.sh`, the `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit` layout, the merge-driver registration and `--harness` behave identically on macOS is **unverified, and nothing in the design claims it**.
  · **A TARBALL install is in use** (`0ec473e`), a different update route from a checkout. `user-iterative-release-preference` sets the goal at a ONE-WORD UPDATE; whether the tarball route reaches that is untested.

⭐ THE BREADTH IS ITSELF THE FINDING: the second user exercises reflow2 across two agents (Claude, Grok) and two project classes (work, personal) on one OS reflow2 has never been tested on. For evidence purposes his two report streams should be read as **two users**, and the two agents mean the served skills are being read by two different models.
